{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Surfaced 2026-08-05 by Anthony's multi-project question, and it is the half his framing exposes that no existing node covers.

⭐ THE GAP. His stated benefit is that "a set of projects done in this manner can ALL INFLUENCE EACH OTHER." Everything reflow2 has built for crossing a design boundary shares CONTRACTS: `cap:publish-surface` publishes "just the boundary — the contracts others may rely on, and nothing internal", `cap:mirror-surface` brings the other side's published surface in as local nodes carrying a coordinate, and `cap:seam-incompatibility` says when two linked designs disagree at that boundary. ALL OF IT IS ABOUT INTERFACES. NOTHING CARRIES A DECISION OR A REQUIREMENT ACROSS. So two of his projects can be checked for whether they fit together, and still know nothing about why the other was built the way it was.

THAT IS PROBABLY NOT WHAT HE MEANS BY INFLUENCE. A ruling made in project_x — "we settled that outdoor units send cumulative totals, so a lost reading heals itself" — is exactly the kind of thing that should reach project_y, and it is not a contract. Neither is a requirement he holds across everything he builds. `dec:nested-graphs` deliberately made foreignness "a property of the NODE rather than of the link", which is the mechanism that WOULD carry this — the question is whether anything other than an Interface is allowed to be mirrored.

WHY IT MAY BE DELIBERATE RATHER THAN MISSING, and this is the strongest counter: `cap:publish-surface`'s whole point is "and nothing internal". A Decision is the most internal thing a design holds — it is the reasoning, the alternatives, the roads not taken. Publishing it is a much larger act than publishing a contract, and a boundary that leaks reasoning may not be a boundary at all. `dec:nested-graphs` chose ownership as the discriminator precisely so a design could share ONE part without sharing everything; letting intent cross could dissolve that.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) NOTHING CROSSES BUT CONTRACTS — today's behaviour, made explicit. Cheapest and defensible; the counter is that it answers Anthony's question with "you cannot have what you asked for" and he should hear that plainly rather than discover it. (b) A DESIGN MAY PUBLISH SELECTED DECISIONS AND REQUIREMENTS, not only Interfaces — publication stays deliberate, so nothing leaks, but the publishable set widens. Counter: `export_surface` and the surface vocabulary would need to say WHAT KIND of thing is published, and the mirrored copy raises a hard question nobody has answered — is a mirrored Decision still binding on the mirroring design, or only visible to it? (c) A STANDING "HOUSE RULES" DESIGN that his projects all mirror — one design holding the intent he carries everywhere (how he works, what he always requires), which every project mirrors and none owns. Fits the accepted rule cleanly, because that design IS separately owned and separately shared. Counter: nothing in reflow2 models a design with no build, and it is close to (d) on `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` without being the same thing. (d) DO NOT SOLVE IT IN THE GRAPH — this is what a person carries between their own projects, and the graph should not try to. Counter: that is the argument this whole product exists to reject, since "the person remembers" is what fails at eighteen months (`req:no-idea-goes-quiet`, accepted the same day).

NOT VERIFIED: whether `export_surface`/`mirror_surface` are structurally limited to Interfaces or merely conventionally used that way. If the mechanism is already general, (b) may be a vocabulary question rather than a build.

⚠️ AND THE PREREQUISITE THAT BOUNDS ALL OF IT: reflow2's own `maturity_report` puts SEAMS at 0 OF 73 — not one coupling in this design runs through a declared Interface that one side provides and the other consumes. So the machinery every option here builds on has never been exercised on the design that ships it, which is the same "self-host cannot see it" shape that hid [BL-176] for eleven releases and produced [BL-213] this morning. Any answer here should be trialled on two real designs before it is believed.","name":"OPEN — mirroring shares CONTRACTS; should INTENT cross a design boundary too, which is what "projects influence each other" actually asks for?","rationale":"Recorded separately from `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` because that node asks WHERE the boundary goes and this one asks WHAT MAY CROSS IT. They travel together and are answered differently: a person could put everything in one graph and still want to know whether intent crosses when they later split it.

Kept as a question rather than a proposal because the counter-argument is strong and structural: `cap:publish-surface` exists to publish the boundary "and nothing internal", so widening it is a change to what a design boundary MEANS, not an added feature. That deserves Anthony's word, not an agent's inference from one sentence of his.

The seams-at-zero warning is on the node deliberately. It is the second time in one day that a mechanism has turned out to be unexercised on reflow2's own design, and the first time cost a silent data-loss defect. Naming it here is cheaper than rediscovering it.","status":"proposed"}
